history.period: Believed ancient - Dwapara Yuga per legend (unverified); current structure's date undocumented
history.summary: The Chandi Mandir stands on the Chandigarh-Kalka highway (NH-5) inside the Chandimandir Cantonment, about 15 km from Chandigarh - it is NOT in Chandigarh city and NOT in Chandigarh UT, despite the CSV town (CSV state 'Haryana' is correct). The planned city of Chandigarh and the cantonment both take their names from this shrine of Chandi, the goddess of power. Local legend dates the temple to the Dwapara Yuga, saying the Pandavas worshipped the deity here (one retelling says the goddess blessed Arjuna with victory before the Mahabharata) - all legend, no archaeological dating found. It is regarded locally as a Siddh Peeth (a place where wishes are believed to come true), set against the Shivalik hills beside the Indian Army's Western Command headquarters.

name: Chandi Mandir (Chandi Devi Temple)
town: Panchkula (Chandimandir Cantonment; CSV town 'Chandigarh' is incorrect - ~15 km away)
town_description: Panchkula is a planned city in Haryana adjoining Chandigarh and Mohali (the Tricity), at the foot of the Shivalik hills. The Chandimandir Cantonment, home to the Indian Army's Western Command headquarters, hosts this temple on the NH-5 highway toward Kalka and Himachal Pradesh.

travel.railway: Chandigarh Railway Station - about 15-20 km (verify); Kalka station nearby on the Kalka-Shimla line.
travel.road: On NH-5 Chandigarh-Kalka Highway, about 200 metres from the Himalayan Expressway; ~15 km from Chandigarh, ~10 km from the Mansa Devi shrine; ample parking (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Navratri for the main celebrations (very crowded).
